extracted.intended_audience: prospective and current MFA applicants and students (creative writers considering or enrolled in the Iowa Writers' Workshop)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview and expectations for the University of Iowa Writers' Workshop MFA in Creative Writing, describing curricular structure, residency requirements, community life, visiting faculty, and application timing. Useful for prospective applicants and students planning participation in the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminal degree qualifying to teach
rubrics_metrics.description: The MFA in Creative Writing offers a Master of Fine Arts degree in English, a terminal degree that qualifies graduates to teach creative writing at the college level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies the program prepares students for academic teaching positions and that the degree is recognized as the terminal credential for college-level creative writing instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time residency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The MFA program requires full-time residency in Iowa City.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Residency is required so students can learn from one another and take advantage of university resources; the program is designed for in-person cohort interaction rather than a low-residency or remote model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop as core curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshops are the heart of the MFA degree and a defining element of the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All graduate students take a workshop each semester with one of the program faculty; the workshop functions as a mini-cohort (8–12 writers) and is the primary setting for drafting, peer critique, and iterative revision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workshop group size and participation expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The workshop, a group of 8-12 writers, becomes each student's mini-cohort for the semester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Over the semester every student submits their creative work one or (often) more times to be read and discussed, indicating repeated, intensive critique cycles and expectation of active engagement from each student.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seminars designed to feed creative work
rubrics_metrics.description: Seminars are designed specifically for writers and are intended to feed their creative work and process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each seminar typically focuses on a specific topic relevant to writers honing their craft, offering concentrated study beyond workshop critique (e.g., form, tradition, technique).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to courses beyond the department
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduate students may take classes outside of the department in many fields at the University of Iowa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students can pursue creative courses (screenwriting, bookmaking, translation) or scholarly courses (languages, history, literature) and take professional seminars/training offered by the Graduate College — supporting interdisciplinary development and professionalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Faculty teaching and advising commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Workshop faculty are well-known figures in American letters, but also committed teachers who have spent their careers teaching and advising emerging writers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes mentorship and sustained pedagogical attention from faculty as part of student development; faculty selection and reputation both contribute to the learning environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visiting writers and relationship-building
rubrics_metrics.description: Every year the Workshop brings a number of distinguished writers to Iowa City to teach workshops and seminars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visiting Writer program allows graduate students to build working relationships with established writers at different career stages; these relationships are often meaningful to students as they progress in their literary careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Readings, master classes, and career programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Throughout the semester, writers come to give readings, Q&As, and master classes in the Frank Conroy Reading Room. The 'After the Workshop' series offers students insight into publishing and career options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programming includes opportunities to meet agents (agents ask to visit annually) and gain practical knowledge about publishing and career paths, supplementing craft study with industry exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community engagement and peer-driven activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging with fellow students is key to writers' growth; the community of about 100 writers runs reading series, edits journals, volunteers, and provides mutual support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Students are expected/encouraged to participate in extracurricular literary activities (reading series, editing Black Poetry Review, volunteering), social life, and cross-program engagement (International Writing Program, Nonfiction, Spanish MFA, Translation) to foster a supportive creative ecosystem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohort/admissions scale
rubrics_metrics.description: Twenty to twenty-five new students in each of the two genres come to Iowa City to join the program each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates selective, limited incoming cohorts per genre (fiction and poetry), shaping peer dynamics, resources per student, and competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program prestige and alumni achievements
rubrics_metrics.description: Program highlights include: 30 Pulitzer Prize winners, 21 MacArthur Genius Grant recipients, 19 National Book Award winners, and 8 U.S. Poets Laureate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as evidence of program quality and successful alumni outcomes; useful for applicants evaluating program reputation but not a prescriptive criterion for student work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are due in December each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the basic application deadline; applicants should consult program materials ('Learn more about applying') for full application requirements and materials.
